bull.b: Affirm’s recent step‑change to sustained positive operating and free cash flow (FCF up ~27% TTM and FCF ~78% of net income) creates durable funding optionality. Persistent cash generation supports securitizations, product investment, underwriting cushions, and reduces reliance on volatile capital markets over months.

A meaningful drop in leverage (debt/equity to ~0.30x TTM) and positive ROE (~11.2%) materially lower funding and solvency risk versus recent years. Improved capital structure enhances resilience to credit cycles, eases ABS execution, and increases strategic optionality for investment or opportunistic growth over the medium term.

Rapid merchant expansion (+44% active merchants), a growing Affirm Card (~4.4M cardholders) and rising engagement (>20% transactions per active) reinforce network effects. Large platform partnerships (Shopify, Intuit) and high repeat usage (90%+ returning users) underpin durable GMV growth and favorable unit economics.

bear.b: A TTM revenue decline of ~13.9% raises questions about the durability of top‑line growth even as margins improve. Slower GMV or merchant presentment would force greater reliance on margin expansion and product mix shifts to sustain earnings, increasing execution risk over a 2–6 month horizon.

Scale of merchant‑funded 0% (Pay‑in‑4 / Pay‑in‑X) products creates structural margin risk: these offers deliver lower RLTC margins versus interest‑bearing loans. If the company grows primarily through lower‑margin 0% programs, sustaining overall unit economics will require higher volumes or offsetting credit/funding improvements.

The larger amended revolving facility carries covenants, leverage and tangible net‑worth tests and triggers tied to convertible notes. These restrictions can limit financing flexibility, constrain strategic moves or borrowing capacity, and introduce acceleration risk if performance or covenant metrics weaken in coming quarters.
